# Test fixtures

## APNG synthetic fixtures

All files in `apng/` are original, deterministic AniView test data generated by
`tools/apng/generate-fixtures.mjs`, using Node's zlib PNG compression and explicit
PNG CRCs. There is no copied artwork or third-party binary content. Fixture data
may be reused under CC0-1.0. Regenerate with Node 24:

```sh
node tools/apng/generate-fixtures.mjs
```

The encoded images follow the [W3C PNG/APNG specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/png-3/).
Most canvases are 3×2 pixels, enabling exact full-frame RGBA assertions in the
real-worker browser check. `expectations.json` records manually specified canvas
results and container metadata, independently of the application compositor.
Alpha-blended colors may differ by one channel unit after browser premultiplication.

| File | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `full-infinite.png` | Default PNG image included as frame 0; two full frames; 20/40ms; infinite loop |
| `full-finite.png` | Two full frames; two total plays |
| `composition.png` | Partial rectangles, offsets, transparent SOURCE, alpha OVER, NONE, BACKGROUND and PREVIOUS |
| `hidden-default.png` | Magenta default PNG image excluded; animation begins on transparent canvas with partial frames |
| `first-previous.png` | First-frame PREVIOUS must behave as BACKGROUND |
| `delays.png` | Zero duration, zero denominator (100), 1ms duration and one total play |
| `static.png` | Ordinary PNG, no `acTL` |
| `long-bounded.png` | 100 frames, 64×64, 100ms, infinite loop; cache-bound observation |

Parser tests also mutate chunk lengths, CRCs, frame counts, rectangles, sequence
numbers and operations. These corrupt variants are generated in test memory,
keeping repository fixtures small.

## External desktop samples (downloaded, ignored)

The real-world integration sample `.tools/fixtures/bouncing-beach-ball.png` is
Holger Will's public-domain [bouncing beach ball](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Animated_PNG_example_bouncing_beach_ball.png):
63,435 bytes, 100×100, 20 frames, 75ms/frame, infinite loop. Downloaded through
the [apngasm-python sample mirror](https://api.github.com/repos/laggykiller/apngasm-python/contents/samples/input/ball.apng),
whose upstream documentation credits Wikimedia Commons. Git blob:
`1b35084a369ee5d40908a70e01ca47fccb144ce4`.
SHA-256: `ce0905f339f44370c0fecc226ef4b422d86f06a3ec4f194e5cfb9d0b50aafb2e`.

An additional [Web Platform Tests sample](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/images/apng.png)
is downloaded as `.tools/fixtures/wpt-apng.png`: 259 bytes, 100×50, two 11ms
frames, one total play. It is subject to the WPT BSD 3-clause license.
SHA-256: `76c3568f8dbf0adcdf15d8a42acd96815ccf317d566118d569c218725167d0a0`.

Neither downloaded binary is committed. These real external samples supplement
the committed synthetic conformance fixtures rather than replacing their pixel
assertions. Measured desktop results are not Android performance claims.

## GIF fixtures

`gif/` contains original CC0-1.0 synthetic pixel patterns, generated with
`node tools/gif-generate.mjs` using omggif's writer only in test tooling.
Cases cover GIF87a without GCE, global/local/local-only palettes, transparent
indices, partial rectangles, disposal 0/1/2/3, absent/finite/infinite loops,
raw delays 0/1/2cs and a 100-frame stream. The 3x4 interlace fixture reproduces
omggif's short-image bug. `interlace-1` through `interlace-17` add offsets,
transparency and local palettes across the four passes. Unit expectations are
independent; browser tests also compare every small frame against Chromium.
Malformed variants and resource-limit cases are generated in memory.

Ignored desktop sample `.tools/fixtures/rotating-earth.gif` is Marvel's
[Rotating earth (large)](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rotating_earth_(large).gif),
downloaded unchanged from
`https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2c/Rotating_earth_%28large%29.gif`.
It is licensed [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)
(also GFDL), and is not distributed in the application or Git.
1,001,718 bytes, 400x400, 44 frames; 65,535 repeats normalize to 65,536 total
plays. SHA-256:
`b0acdc9a01f91f6123dbff38d4bee59d0d6e4b26071b5c83937b242b6b202378`.

## ZIP fixtures

`zip/` contains original tiny CC0-1.0 test archives created by
`node tools/archive/generate-fixtures.mjs` using the pinned zip.js writer only
in test tooling. Their media are the original GIF/APNG patterns above and a
2×2 red/green two-frame WebP assembled from original lossless canvas-encoded
solid pixels (`original-two-frame.webp`). No downloaded artwork is committed.
ZIP writer timestamps are fixed; encryption salts/headers remain randomized,
so encrypted archives reproduce the same contents and metadata, not ciphertext.
The deliberately public test password is `AniView-test`; it is never a user
password and is not part of application password storage.

The corpus covers empty, individual GIF/WebP/APNG, mixed central-directory
order, nested directories, macOS metadata, no media, wrong/missing extensions,
unsafe paths, Zip64, ZipCrypto, AES, mixed encrypted/public entries, damaged
payload CRC, unsupported compression, truncated headers/directories, oversized
declared output, and extreme declared compression ratio. `manifest.json`
records entry sizes and generation metadata. Mutated ZIPs are test inputs,
not valid examples for users.

`node tools/archive/generate-fixtures.mjs --large` additionally creates ignored
`.tools/fixtures/archive-large.zip` with 60 entries repeating the three existing
downloaded desktop samples (WebP, APNG, GIF). The external sources and licenses
remain those recorded above and in the WebP milestone documentation; neither
the archive nor extracted test media is committed. This smoke test checks
current-only extraction and UI responsiveness without multi-gigabyte media.
